findings.title: "No edits to 424 or 425" contradicts the rest of the document, and some text is left over from an earlier revision
findings.description:
Line 42 says this slice makes no edits to 424 or 425. Other parts of the same document say it edits both:
- **425's `bench_report.py`:** it gains per-kind grouping and the pairwise section (lines 87 and 427, D17).
- **424's `CaseDrop.reason`:** it is widened to accept `SliceCandidateRejection` (lines 321 and 426).
- **`tests/benchmark/`:** line 451 says these tests pass unchanged "except where D8 routes re-qualification and D17 extracts the interval."

Line 451 also conflicts with the decisions themselves. D8 (line 225) uses the `requalify` seam 424 already has; 424 D208 confirms that `replay_one` calls only `runner.requalify`, so `bench_runner.py` needs no change. D17 (line 312) says `bootstrap_mean_interval` already exists in 425 (425 D14) and that 425 is not changed. So nothing in D8 or D17 changes routing or extracts an interval. Line 451 looks left over from an earlier draft.

A task writer reading these lines could plan edits that aren't needed, or skip edits that are. To fix:
- Change line 42 to list the real touch points: `bench_report` grouping and the pairwise section, `CaseDrop.reason` widening, and `yield_report` rows.
- Change line 451 to name the tests that actually change: report tests for the per-kind tables, and `CaseDrop` model tests.

findings.title: Covers every item the slice plan entry assigns
findings.description:
Each success criterion in the plan's 426 entry is covered:
- Cases build from 400/403 slice ranges, and every exclusion has a recorded reason (D1–D6).
- Replays run through producer-only `P6` (D8).
- Slice cases get tables separate from fix cases (D17).
- The judge sees only normalized diffs (D11).
- The reference is a reference line, never ranked (D17).
- The over-size rule is stated and counted (D14).

The plan left the diff-size rule open. D14 settles it: an over-size case is excluded and counted, nothing is truncated, and the reason for rejecting a bounded view is given. That meets the architecture's requirement of "a stated rule ... not silent truncation." Nothing assigned to this slice is dropped or deferred. Reviewer recall and non-Python languages are excluded, and both belong to other slices or Future Work.

findings.title: Follows the architecture's principles
findings.description:
- **Objective before opinion:** the pairwise result is reported beside the objective grade and never folded into it, with no composite (D17, line 313).
- **Absent is not zero:** config absences forfeit their pairs, and harness absences drop the case (D15).
- **No slice tests as hidden tests:** nodes that exist only at the tip are ignored (D5).
- **Extend 320's store:** new records are sibling payloads with no migration, and diffs are sidecars.
- **Mechanical qualification:** every rejection reason is recorded (D6).
- **Production pipelines:** replays run producer-only `P6` and do not copy it.

Dependencies point the right way. The slice reaches the language only through 422's adapter registry, and adds `SliceCaseRunner` through 424's seam without editing the runner.

findings.title: The reference is the slice branch tip, not the landing commit the architecture names
findings.description: The architecture's Envisioned State says "the landing commit is the reference." D2 uses `tip_sha` instead, and rejects slices whose branch contains merges. The reason given is sound: on a merge landing, `fork..after` also contains unrelated work from the target. This is a justified refinement, not a violation. The architecture could be updated to match.

findings.title: The judge can spend calls on cases already dropped at grading
findings.description: D15 removes cases dropped at grading (`reference_failed_grade`, grading harness absences) only at report time. `sq benchmark judge` looks only at replay harness absences before it dispatches, so those cases still get judge calls. The calls show in the printed bound, so spend stays visible, but the money buys nothing. If grade records exist when `judge` runs, it could skip those cases cheaply.

findings.title: The judge cap uses 425's per-command caps, not one run-level cap
findings.description: The architecture says one run-level cap "covers all of it": replays, grading and judging. D16 follows 425's pattern instead, with a separate required `--max-cost` for each command. Line 148 calls it the "run cap", and the bound example says "capped at run cap $8.00" while showing the `--max-cost` value. That makes it unclear whether the slice means the cap stored on the `BenchmarkRun` or the flag. It is also unclear whether a resumed `judge` counts spend from earlier invocations. This comes from 425, so it isn't this slice's to fix, but the slice could use one term consistently.

findings.title: `--keep` on `slice-cases build` is not explained
findings.description: The CLI signature includes `--keep`, but nothing in the document says what it keeps. It probably means keeping qualification sandboxes, as in 422. Define it in one line or remove it.

findings.title: Failure modes are covered for each new I/O path
findings.description:
Each new path has explicit handling that can be observed:
- **cf registration steps:** a failure is a harness absence, logged at ERROR with the step and its stderr (D9).
- **`git` calls in discovery or qualification:** a failure or timeout is a `harness_error`, logged at ERROR, and never charged to the slice (D6).
- **Judge calls:** bounded by `metrology.judge_timeout_s`. A failed pair is left unrecorded, logged at ERROR, counted, and retried on the next run (D15).
- **A `tip_sha` missing from `--repo`:** `judge` refuses and names the case and sha.
- **Cap reached:** judging stops with exit 2 and keeps every record.
- **Over-size prompt:** the case is recorded as `OverSizeCase` and counted.

Success Criteria (line 443) requires a test asserting the signal for each of these. The risk that cf may not work under a scrubbed home is handled by a spike that runs first and stops the slice with a `BLOCKED:` line if the answer is no.

findings.title: The spend-visibility requirement is restated with concrete targets
findings.description:
The architecture's goal, "spend is visible before it happens", is restated concretely for judging:
- `--max-cost` is required.
- The per-call cost figure comes from the largest observed call cost, or from a flag, and the command refuses when neither exists.
- The bound prints before any dispatch and includes a one-call overshoot.
- The cap is checked before each call.

The bound example shows how the pair count, the forfeit count and the over-size and harness-absent exclusions feed into it.

findings.title: Size is proportionate
findings.description: Each mechanism maps to a requirement in the architecture or the slice plan. The design reuses existing pieces rather than rebuilding them: 422's adapter and `test_sets`, 425's grader and bootstrap, 177's judge core and Bradley-Terry fit. Two extractions (`CfRegistration`, `judge_pair`) avoid duplicating code. D13 judges only sample-matched cross-config pairs plus replay-vs-reference pairs, which takes 9 pairs instead of 21 at two configs and k = 3. `with_tools` is as small as it can be, and fix cases never use it. Nothing I found should be cut. Effort 3/5 matches the slice plan.
